predecessors.name: Harsha's Empire (Pushyabhuti dynasty)
predecessors.text: Harsha's realm, 606-647 on the Kannauj page, from which Yashovarman seized power after Harsha died without an heir

ledger.x: 725: Yashovarman founds the Varman dynasty at Kannauj (Kanyakubja).

c. 740: the Kashmiri alliance breaks and Lalitaditya attacks Kannauj. The Yashovarman page: the alliance with Muktapida, with whom he had defeated the Tibetans, collapsed around 740; Majumdar says Lalitaditya defeated him and annexed his lands, Tripathi that he may have stayed on the throne after a nominal…

c. 741: the war ends with Yashovarman still reigning. The Lalitaditya page: Kalhana has him submit 'after a long war and offered a peace treaty', Mishra that he acknowledged Lalitaditya's suzerainty 'for a short period' and became practically independent later; no year for the end. The end year is bridging: Cliopatria…
770: Vajrayudha deposes the Varmans and the Ayudha dynasty rules Kannauj.
771: the Varman realm is reduced to the Kannauj core.

c. 786: Dhruva of the Rashtrakutas marches on Kannauj. The Tripartite Struggle page has Dhruva defeat Vatsaraja and then Dharmapala in the Doab, only meant to raid, not conquer; the Pratihara page dates his crossing of the Narmada and attempt on Kannauj c. 786. This page…

wars.name: Yashovarman and Lalitaditya's alliance against the Tibetans
wars.outcome: The Yashovarman page says he was briefly allied with Muktapida and the two defeated the Tibetans; no land is said to have changed hands.

wars.name: War of Lalitaditya and Yashovarman
wars.outcome: Kalhana: Yashovarman submitted after a long war and was then uprooted; modern historians differ on whether Kannauj was annexed (Majumdar) or Yashovarman stayed on his throne after a nominal acknowledgement of supremacy (Tripathi, Mishra).

wars.name: Tripartite Struggle
wars.outcome: Pratihara victory in 816: Nagabhata II defeats Chakrayudha, Dharmapala's nominee, and proclaims himself king of Kannauj; the Ayudha dynasty ends.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page; the extent of the kingdom is a poem's claim (Gaudavaho) before 770 and a minimal Kannauj-and-Doab reading after.
